subject: math
label: Limits
blurb: JEE Main to JEE Advanced limits practice: verified-style questions plus original challenge problems graded by difficulty and tagged by technique.

toolkit.title: Small-x replacements
toolkit.desc: Near \(x\to0\), swap these in before simplifying — only leading order matters: \(\sin kx \to kx\), \(\tan kx \to kx\), \(1-\cos kx \to \tfrac{k^2x^2}{2}\), \(\ln(1+kx) \to kx\), \(e^{kx}-1 \to kx\).

toolkit.title: When leading terms cancel, go deeper
toolkit.desc: If the substitution above kills the whole expression, use the next Taylor term: \(\sin x\approx x-\tfrac{x^3}{6}\), \(\tan x\approx x+\tfrac{x^3}{3}\), \(\cos x\approx1-\tfrac{x^2}{2}+\tfrac{x^4}{24}\).

toolkit.title: A power raised to a function, exponentiated
toolkit.desc: Never expand \([1+f(x)]^{g(x)}\) directly. Isolate \(f(x)\to0\) and \(g(x)\to\infty\), take that product's limit, and exponentiate: \([1+f(x)]^{g(x)} \to e^{\lim f(x)g(x)}\).

toolkit.title: Memorize the big expansions
toolkit.desc: \((1+x)^{1/x}=e(1-\tfrac x2+\tfrac{11x^2}{24}-\cdots)\) and its generalization show up constantly — know them cold.

toolkit.title: Roots of a quadratic? Use Vieta's
toolkit.desc: If \(\alpha,\beta\) are roots of \(ax^2+bx+c=0\), express symmetric answers via \(\alpha+\beta=-b/a\) and \(\alpha\beta=c/a\) directly.

toolkit.title: Telescoping — spot the subtraction shape
toolkit.desc: \(\tan^{-1}\) sums or partial fractions like \(\tfrac{1}{r(r+1)}\) are usually a disguised \(g(r+1)-g(r)\). Rewrite before summing.

toolkit.title: Limits at infinity with unknowns
toolkit.desc: Do the polynomial division first. Whatever coefficient multiplies a divergent power of \(x\) must be forced to zero.

toolkit.title: Matching orders in 0/0 with parameters
toolkit.desc: Force the lower-order coefficient to vanish first (fixes one unknown), then read the remaining ratio off the next surviving terms.

toolkit.title: Radical differences — substitute
toolkit.desc: For \(\sqrt[3]{a^3+x}-a\)-type expressions, let \(y=\) the root expression. It becomes a difference-of-squares/cubes factoring problem.

toolkit.title: Recognize the derivative definition
toolkit.desc: \(\lim_{h\to0}\tfrac{f(a+h)-f(a)}{h}\) (in any variable name) is just \(f'(a)\). Spotting this skips all algebra.

toolkit.title: Sums that are secretly Riemann sums
toolkit.desc: \(\tfrac1n\sum f(k/n)\to\int_0^1 f(x)dx\) — convert to an integral. Use closed forms for \(\sum r,\ \sum r^2,\ \sum r^3\) instead of summing.

toolkit.title: Check indeterminacy first
toolkit.desc: If plugging in the point directly gives a real number, you're done — no L'Hôpital, no expansion needed. Most commonly skipped step.

toolkit.title: 0/0 at a “nice” nonzero point → L'Hôpital
toolkit.desc: Series expansions are for \(x\to0\). At points like \(\pi/4\) or \(1\), differentiating top and bottom is almost always faster.

toolkit.title: Denominator → 0, numerator doesn't
toolkit.desc: Check the sign of each factor just left and right of the point separately — don't assume \(\pm\infty\) blindly; it may be a genuine DNE.

toolkit.title: Rational end behavior — compare degrees
toolkit.desc: deg(denominator) > deg(numerator) ⇒ limit is 0. Equal degrees ⇒ ratio of leading coefficients. No expansion needed.

toolkit.title: Closed-form sums, not hand summation
toolkit.desc: \(\sum r,\ \sum r^2,\ \sum r^3,\ \sum(2r-1)=n^2\), and \(\sum ar^k=\tfrac{ar}{1-r}\) for \(|r|<1\) — recall the formula, don't expand term by term.

toolkit.title: Fixed-point recurrences
toolkit.desc: For a convergent recurrence \(a_{n+1}=f(a_n)\to L\), solve \(L=f(L)\) directly instead of tracking terms.

toolkit.title: Infinite products & functional iteration
toolkit.desc: Take \(\ln\) to turn a product into a sum (often a Riemann sum), or recognize repeated angle-halving products collapsing to \(\tfrac{\sin x}{x}\).

items: Riemann sum (0 to 1): \(\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\dfrac1n\sum_{k=1}^n f\!\left(\dfrac kn\right)=\int_0^1 f(x)dx\)
